newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX markets close for holidays.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX markets close for holidays.

text.p: SIMEX futures markets were closed on Wednesday for the New Year holiday. SIMEX trades half day for Euroyen and Eurodollar on Thursday, a public holiday for Singapore's general election.
On Tuesday SIMEX Euroyen futures ended a tad softer in lacklustre activity ahead of the New Year holiday, while Eurodollars stayed unchanged.
Trade was mostly driven by U.S. funds adjusting positions, and local dealers punting over the thinly traded session.
Japanese financial markets are closed for a week-long break and trade will resume next week on January 6.
The June contract ended at 99.39 against the IMM's previous 99.40 close, with September at 99.24, down from 99.25.
Profit taking was also being pursued on views Euroyen had risen strongly in recent days due to weak stock prices, and that there would be no incentive to change interest rates.
Operators suggested that a bearish yen, which set a new high in Asia today at 116.28 to the dollar, should lend Euroyen support when the market resumes trading in earnest next week.
The Nikkei 225 index recouped losses ahead of its close on Monday, before Japan's week-long shutdown, but traders were unconvinced it could sustain 19,000 points in the new year.
But others said a weaker yen could be beneficial for Japan's trade surplus in the longer-term.
Eurodollar futures were unchanged in subdued dealings with U.S. economic data causing no major stir, dealers said.
Japanese Government Bonds (JGB) futures were untraded with Tokyo markets closed. On Monday, the March contract ended lower at 124.11, down 37 points, with critical support at 124.0.
